root_cause.text: The `xfrm6_rcv_encap()` function in the IPv6 xfrm subsystem fails to release the reference to the `dst` entry obtained from `ip6_route_input_lookup()` when the lookup returns an error route, resulting in a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `dst_release(dst);` inside the `if (dst->error)` block in `net/ipv6/xfrm6_protocol.c`, correcting the behavior described in the CVE where the code drops the skb "without releasing the reference returned by the lookup."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes a memory leak in xfrm6_rcv_encap by properly releasing the dst_entry reference upon route lookup failure.
intent_record.what: Wrapped the if (dst->error) check in braces and added a call to dst_release(dst) before the goto drop statement.
intent_record.how: Ensures the reference count of the destination entry is decremented when the route lookup fails, preventing a memory leak of the dst_entry structure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This declaration introduces the dst_entry pointer that will hold the result from ip6_route_input_lookup(). When the lookup returns an error route, the subsequent code fails to call dst_release() on this pointer before returning, causing a memory leak. The vulnerability occurs because the dst reference acquired from the route lookup is not properly released in error paths.
